newsitem.title: UK: UK, France to promote democracy, trade in Africa.
newsitem.headline: UK, France to promote democracy, trade in Africa.

text.p: Britain and France agreed on Wednesday to join forces to promote democracy and economic development in Africa.
British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said he discussed Africa at some length at his first full face-to-face meeting with his French counterpart, Hubert Vedrine.
European monetary union and enlargement also featured prominently at what Cook said had been a successful meeting that laid a firm foundation for closer ties.

"We have agreed on a programme of cooperation in our work in Africa in order that we can support each other in trying to raise the levels of democracy in Africa and also to promote economic development, particularly in trade with Europe," Cook, flanked by Vedrine, told reporters.
"We strongly believe that if France and Britain cooperate in Africa, it will not only be better for our countries but it will also be much better for the countries of Africa," he added.

British officials said Cook wanted to work with Paris to see how they could apply the general principles of democracy and good government laid down by the Commonwealth, which groups Britain and its colonies, and the Francophonie club of French-speaking countries.
Cook, who is determined to put human rights at the heart of Britain's foreign policy, also discussed with Vedrine his goal of reaching a European Union code of conduct on the arms trade.

He said he had told Vedrine that Britain was unlikely to be in the first wave of countries to join the EU's single currency but, as EU president in the first half of 1998, would do its duty so those countries that want to sign up can do so.
